also: to the best of my ability
to the best of one’s ability

terms.gloss: ability, capacity; the means or chance to do something
terms.comment: With a gerund in the genitive for what one can do: dīcendī facultās, the ability to speak; legendī scrībendīque facultās, the ability to read and write (Traupman 267). To the best of my ability, prō meā parte (Traupman 92, 267), or Livy’s prō virīlī parte (praef. 3).

terms.gloss: the power or possibility of doing something
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. potestās: “ability, power of doing any thing (class.)”
terms.comment: More often the power one is given, or an opportunity, than an ability one has.

terms.gloss: for my (your, his) part, to the best of my ability
to the best of one’s ability, as far as one can
evidence: Cic. Sest. 138; Liv. praef. 2 (Lewis & Short s.v. pars)
terms.comment: The stronger form: literally “for a man’s share”.

terms.gloss: as hard as one can, with all one’s strength

phrases.latin: īnfantēs ā mūtīs nūtrīcibus jussū rēgum in sōlitūdine ēducātī, etiamsī verba quaedam ēmīsisse trāduntur, tamen loquendī facultāte caruērunt
phrases.english: babies brought up in solitude by mute nurses on the orders of kings, though they are said to have uttered some words, still lacked the ability to speak

phrases.latin: neque longiōra mihi darī spatia vīvendī volō quam dum erō ad hanc quoque facultātem scrībendī commentandīque idōneus
phrases.english: and I want no longer span of life than while I am still able to write and take notes

phrases.latin: juvābit tamen rērum gestārum memoriae prīncipis terrārum populī prō virīlī parte et ipsum cōnsuluisse
phrases.english: still, it will be a pleasure to have done, to the best of my ability, my own part for the memory of the deeds of the foremost people on earth
the ability to read and write
